habitat: Open savanna, woodland edge and game country; often near carcasses with other large eagles and vultures (Newman's; Wikipedia).
summary: A large, dark brown Palearctic migrant eagle with fully feathered legs. Adult is plain dark brown with orange-yellow gape and feet; the long gape line extending beyond the centre of the eye separates it from Tawny Eagle (Newman's; Wikipedia).

similar.note: Tawny Eagle is resident, often paler/tawny or mottled; gape does not extend as far past the eye centre; oval vs round nostril differences also cited (Wikipedia; Newman's).
Lesser Spotted Eagle is smaller (~65 cm) with narrowly feathered 'stovepipe' legs; immatures show white spots on the folded wings (Newman's).

viewNotes.note: Uniform dark brown with long yellow gape line and feathered legs (Newman's; Wikipedia).
Dark underwing; exact pale panels vary with age. Compare carefully with Tawny and Lesser Spotted (Wikipedia).

calls.description: Generally silent on the non-breeding grounds in southern Africa; open recordings available are mostly from the Palearctic breeding range.

research.note: Status is stored as palearctic-migrant. The research treated this as a Palearctic summer visitor, which is the same movement, and palearctic-migrant is the status this site already uses. No breeding plumage change in Africa; age-related plumage variation is substantial. Gaps: Few Kruger-labelled Commons photos; many Steppe Eagle images are from Asia. Sexes alike; no sexed images. Quiet in Africa — local call recordings scarce. Photos left out: A repeated file was omitted. GBIF Kruger months peak Oct–Mar (Palearctic summer visitor). Confusion with dark Tawny Eagles is a known field problem. monthsPresent set from Newman/SABAP seasonality cross-checked with GBIF Kruger month facets (not abundance).
